entries.proven_relationships: Field conversion trait and integer macro implementations form a separate conversion contract. to_reflected_value does not apply Runtime recursive budget and need not establish finite floats. Conversion errors do not replace ReflectedValue graph validation.

Runtime sets depth 128, nodes 16384, string bytes 1 MiB, per-container entries 4096. Borrowed values use validate_with_budget; field-facing wrapper maps rejection to ReflectError::InvalidValue with type/field context. Each field is checked independently; graph budgets do not establish schema/permission correctness.

Versioned or historical schema-zero JSON is loaded before the constructed ReflectedValue is budget-validated. The budget does not cap JSON parser input bytes or allocation that occurred before validation.
Validates the borrowed graph before cloning it into a versioned JSON document and serializing. Validation failure prevents that serialization; schema and authorization remain separate concerns.

In reflected object validation, duplicate source fields are rejected before the current field value is graph-validated under the Runtime budget. Graph rejection carries type and field context through VmStateMigrationError::ReflectedValueRejected. Each value validation borrows input and keeps local budget state.

Target type indexing and schema default validation route present default values through the same Runtime graph budget. Fields without defaults are skipped; rejection includes target type and field. This is distinct from UiBindingValue::validate_with_budget.

Forbidden Runtime source-path substrings are gated by the actual Rust-code-position scanner. // comments set line_comment and are excluded before newline; budget source paths in documentation do not by themselves violate this guard.
